Effective Date: November 17, 2026  |  Last Reviewed: November 17, 2026  |  Supervised By: TopBlogTech Standards & Review Desk

This document establishes the operational rules, research standards, review methodologies, and transparency mandates governing all technical analysis and reporting on TopBlogTech.com.

edits.find:
Fact-Checking Process

At TopBlogTech.com, fact-checking is not an afterthought; it is integrated into every phase of the publication lifecycle. Our editorial workflow incorporates a rigorous, four-stage verification protocol before any article or technical update goes live.

  1. Stage 1 — Source Verification & Technical Synthesis: The author maps every quantitative claim, benchmark statistic, software capability, and pricing tier to a verified primary source link or official documentation archive.
  2. Stage 2 — Technical Peer Review: A member of our technical editorial desk reviews the draft specifically to test code snippets, verify syntax, confirm command line interface (CLI) commands, and check that software architectural designs adhere to modern best practices.
  3. Stage 3 — Copy Editing & Standards Compliance: Our copy editors audit the content for clarity, tone, readability, logical flow, heading structure, and adherence to our internal style guide, ensuring the absence of hyperbole, promotional spin, or sensationalized headlines.
  4. Stage 4 — Compliance & Disclosure Verification: Before publication, the final draft is inspected to confirm appropriate affiliate disclosure notices, correct internal and external citation hyperlinks, schema markup validation, and compliance with our publishing ethics.

Any article containing unsubstantiated claims or code examples that fail technical replication is immediately returned to the author for revision or rejected entirely.
edits.replace:
Pre-Publication Checklist

TopBlogTech has no separate fact-checking team. Before a guide is published or substantially updated, the site owner works through this checklist:

  1. Sources: every statistic, limit, policy statement and price is linked to a primary or reliable published source, or removed.
  2. Currency: product names, versions, policies and plan details are checked against the current official documentation.
  3. Technical steps: commands, settings and code snippets are compared with the official documentation they come from. Readers should still test changes in a safe environment before applying them to a live site.
  4. Claims and tone: no first-hand testing claims, guaranteed results, income promises or sensational headlines.
  5. Links and disclosures: internal and external links work, and any commercial relationship (none at present) is disclosed.

Reader reports are an important second check. If you find something that does not hold up, please tell us (see below).

edits.find:
Author Guidelines

Every contributor to TopBlogTech.com is expected to embody high journalistic integrity and demonstrated technical competence. We hold our writers and technical analysts to rigorous professional benchmarks:

  • Demonstrated Technical Subject Matter Expertise: Contributors must possess verifiable, real-world experience in the domains they cover, including software development, systems administration, technical search engine optimization, cloud infrastructure, or digital publishing.
  • Transparent Author Attribution: We believe in transparent accountability. Articles are published under clear author bylines accompanied by biographical profiles detailing the author's background, credentials, professional experience, and areas of expertise.
  • Mandatory Conflict of Interest Disclosures: Authors are strictly required to disclose any financial interest, equity holding, prior employment, or consulting arrangement with any entity, software vendor, or competitor covered in their work. Authors with material conflicts of interest are disqualified from reviewing the affected products.
  • Responsible Generative AI Policy: We recognize generative artificial intelligence as a valuable tool for research synthesis, code formatting, structural outlining, and syntax debugging. However, TopBlogTech.com strictly prohibits the automated publishing of raw, uncurated, or hallucinated AI outputs. Every article must be conceptualized, drafted, fact-checked, tested, and approved by human subject-matter experts who assume personal responsibility for its technical veracity.
edits.replace:
Authorship and Use of AI Tools

  • One responsible author: All content is published under the responsibility of the founder, Deepak Pandey. There are no staff writers or other contributors at present; if guest contributions are ever accepted, they will be clearly attributed.
  • Conflicts of interest: If the site owner has a financial relationship with a company covered in a guide, it will be disclosed in that guide.
  • AI tools: AI writing tools may be used to help with research, outlining and drafting. AI output is not published as-is: facts are checked against linked sources, unsupported claims are removed, and the site owner is responsible for everything published.
